walkthrough:
Use the identity $\sin^2 2\theta = 1 - \cos^2 2\theta$ to write the equation in terms of $\cos 2\theta$:
$$3(1 - \cos^2 2\theta) + 8\cos 2\theta = 0 \implies 3 - 3\cos^2 2\theta + 8\cos 2\theta = 0$$
$$3\cos^2 2\theta - 8\cos 2\theta - 3 = 0$$

Set the valid factor equal to zero (since $|\cos 2\theta| \le 1$):
$$\cos 2\theta = -\frac{1}{3}$$

Find both solutions for $2\theta$ in the interval $0^\circ \le 2\theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$2\theta_1 = 180^\circ - \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = 180^\circ - 70.53^\circ = 109.47^\circ \implies \theta_1 \approx 54.7^\circ$$
$$2\theta_2 = 360^\circ - 109.47^\circ = 250.53^\circ \implies \theta_2 \approx 125.3^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = 54.7^\circ, \quad 125.3^\circ)$$

hints: Substitute $(0, \sqrt{3})$ into $y = a + \tan bx$ to find $a = \sqrt{3}$.
walkthrough:
Substitute the $y$-intercept $(0, \sqrt{3})$ into the curve equation $y = a + \tan bx$:
$$\sqrt{3} = a + \tan(b \times 0) = a + 0 \implies a = \sqrt{3}$$

Solve for the constant $b$ using the principal inverse tangent value:
$$-\frac{b\pi}{6} = -\frac{\pi}{3} \implies \frac{b}{6} = \frac{1}{3} \implies b = 2$$
$$a = \sqrt{3}, \quad b = 2$$
